# GP-0342 · Involution generation of a code automorphism group

**Theorem.** Given a binary linear code together with permutation generators of its full permutation automorphism group, deciding whether this group is generated by its elements of order two is NP-complete. The reduction constructs the code and a complete generating set. On a generator-given permutation group the upper bound applies to generation by elements of any specified prime order.

## Local groups from Boolean constraints

Use a Boolean circuit with AND gates and NOT gates to encode a 3-CNF instance. Introduce a variable for each input and gate value. A gate gives a Boolean equation $z=xy$ or $z=1+x$, and the output has value one. Homogenize by a new variable $x_0$. Replace every constant one by $x_0^2$, every linear term $x_i$ by $x_0x_i$, and every square $x_i^2$ with $i>0$ by $x_0x_i$. This preserves the equation when $x_0=1$. The resulting homogeneous quadratic polynomials $Q_j$ each use at most four variables, including the anchor if needed. They satisfy $Q_j(e_i)=0$ for every $i>0$.

Let $S_j$ contain the variables of $Q_j$, and choose a bilinear form $\beta_j$ on $F_2^{S_j}$ with $\beta_j(u,u)=Q_j(u)$. One may assign each quadratic monomial to one ordered pair of coordinates. Define the constant-size group $H_j=F_2^{S_j}\times F_2$ with law
$$
(u,z)(v,w)=(u+v,z+w+\beta_j(u,v)).
$$
Bilinearity gives associativity. The second coordinate subgroup is central, the quotient by it is elementary abelian, and $(u,z)^2=(0,Q_j(u))$.

Take the subgroup $E$ of $F_2^{n+1}\times\prod_j H_j$ in which each local vector coordinate $u_j$ equals the restriction $x|_{S_j}$ of the common vector $x$. It projects onto every common vector and has elementary abelian central kernel. Explicit generators with common vector $e_i$ and all central coordinates zero, together with one central toggle per equation, generate it. A group element with common vector $x$ has square one exactly when every $Q_j(x)$ is zero. Its class is at most two and its exponent divides four.

Let $I$ be the subgroup of $E$ generated by involutions. It contains the central kernel and its image on the common vector coordinates contains the span of $e_i$ for $i>0$. If the Boolean system is satisfiable, a square-one element with $x_0=1$ is an involution, so $I$ maps onto the full common vector space and equals $E$. Conversely, if $I=E$ then some involution has common coordinate $x_0=1$, since otherwise every element in their generated subgroup would have $x_0=0$. Its quadratic equations recover a satisfying assignment. This proves the equivalence.

## Realizing the group as a graph automorphism group

For each local factor $H_j$, give the graph a distinct color class of vertices indexed by its elements. Inside that block include directed arcs $h\to hs$ of color $(j,s)$ for every $s\ne1$. A color-preserving automorphism on that block commutes with all right translations, so it is exactly a left translation by some $t_j\in H_j$. For each common variable $i$ give the graph a distinct two-vertex color class indexed by $F_2$. Each element vertex $h=(u,z)$ in block $j$ is incident to the bit vertex $u_i$ whenever $i\in S_j$. An automorphism of a bit class is addition by some $x_i$ and an automorphism of a local class adds the vector part of $t_j$ to the label $u$. Incidence is preserved precisely when those local vector parts agree with $x|_{S_j}$. Thus the complete color-preserving automorphism group is $E$, and its above generators have explicit vertex permutations.

For an ordinary simple graph encoding, replace every directed arc by a length-three undirected path whose two internal vertices have distinct colors identifying the arc label and the tail or head role. These paths are internally disjoint. The incidence relations between equation classes and bit classes already give ordinary edges. Every color-preserving automorphism of the old vertices lifts uniquely to the new graph because each ordered colored arc is unique. Remove colors by attaching three pendant paths of distinct lengths $1$, $2$, and $3+c$ to every vertex of color $c\ge0$, counting length by edges. The old vertices now have degree at least three, while every added vertex has degree at most two. The attached path lengths recover the old color. Once an old vertex image is specified, each of its attached paths has a unique map to the target path of equal length. This uncolored simple graph $\Gamma$ therefore has automorphism group $E$, with explicit generators and polynomial size.

## Realizing it in a binary linear code

Let $v$ be the number of vertices of $\Gamma$. Take a binary generator matrix with two copies of $e_i\in F_2^v$ for each vertex and one copy of $e_i+e_j$ for each edge. It has full row rank. The only columns of multiplicity two are the basis columns. A coordinate automorphism therefore induces a row-space linear transformation permuting the basis, and that vertex permutation preserves exactly the edge columns. The kernel permutes the two equal copies independently at each vertex, and copying vertex permutations on the first and second copies separately gives a splitting. Consequently the full permutation automorphism group is $(C_2)^v\rtimes{\rm Aut}(\Gamma)$, and a generating set consists of the lifts of the displayed graph generators and the copy swaps. The kernel is generated by involutions, and every involution in the graph automorphism group has an involution lift in the splitting. The full code group is generated by involutions exactly when its quotient $E$ is. The reduction uses the actual full code automorphism group and supplies its generators.

Finally, a permutation group generated by elements of order $p$ has a generating list of at most $\lfloor\log_2 |G|\rfloor$ such elements. Greedily adjoin one of those elements outside the generated subgroup until all are contained. Each strict inclusion at least doubles subgroup order. For a group of degree $N$, this list has length $O(N\log N)$. Check the orders and the two generator containments by polynomial-time permutation-group arithmetic. This gives the upper bound.

The local square formulas are the quadratic analogue of the compact commutator encoding in the first catalogue packet. The final graph and code translation makes the auxiliary automorphism-group promise explicit. The complexity proof is written.
